topic: Tyres and tubes, variation of tyre pressure with all up weight, creep and creep marking on wheels.
syllabus_extract: Tyres and tubes, variation of tyre pressure with all up weight, creep and creep marking on wheels.
specific_objectives: 9.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to describe various Aircraft engineering systems.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Inspection of wheel assembly for creep marks; verification of pressure against weight chart; safety: wear eye protection and use jack stands.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of aircraft tyres?
How does all-up weight affect tyre pressure requirements?
What visual indication suggests a wheel has undergone creep?

topics: Function of tyre beads and flanges
Role of tyre pressure in load bearing
development.content:
Tyre and tube construction types
Function of tyre beads and flanges
Tubeless versus tubed systems
Material properties of tyre carcass
Role of tyre pressure in load bearing

Pressure variation with all-up weight
Interpretation of pressure/weight charts
Consequences of under-inflation
Consequences of over-inflation
Standard pressure adjustment procedures

topics: Definition and causes of wheel creep
development.content:
Definition and causes of wheel creep
Identification of creep marks
Creep marking application standards
Inspection criteria for creep limits
Maintenance actions for crept wheels

summary_questions: Explain why tyre pressure must increase as all-up weight increases.
Describe the difference between a tubeless and a tubed tyre system.
What maintenance action is required if creep marks exceed allowable limits?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the basic design requirements of a pneumatic system to be discussed in the next lesson (LP 07).

pft_rows.syllabus: Pneumatic system basic design requirements, brief description, advantages and disadvantages of a typical pneumatic system.
